item.title: The Government of Canada invests in stronger, more resilient and affordable food distribution systems
item.description: Today, the Honourable Heath MacDonald, Minister of Agriculture and Agri-Food, and the Honourable Gregor Robertson, Minister of Housing and Infrastructure, announced the upcoming launch of the $1 billion Food-Link Fund, a key component of the $3.2 billion National Food Security Strategy announced by the Prime Minister on June 11, 2026.

item.title: Ministers Alty, Gull-Masty, Chartrand, and Valdez issue a statement on Sisters in Spirit Day and the National Day of Action for Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women, Girls and 2SLGBTQI+ people
item.description: On Sisters in Spirit Day, we honour and remember all the Indigenous women, girls and 2SLGBTQI+ people who have gone missing or been murdered. We stand with the survivors, families, and communities whose advocacy, leadership and determination continue to drive action and accountability, and we recommit ourselves to ending this violence.

item.title: Joint Statement on the Anniversary of the Snapback of UN Restrictions on and related to Iran
item.description: “On September 27, 2025 (at 8:00 p.m. EDT), six United Nations Security Council resolutions (UNSCRs) – 1696 (2006), 1737 (2006), 1747 (2007), 1803 (2008), 1835 (2008), 1929 (2010) – returned into force pursuant to the completion of the snapback process. France, Germany, and the United Kingdom initiated this process in response to Tehran’s persistent and significant non-performance of its nuclear commitments under the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA).

item.title: Government of Canada to implement a transition year before full seed increase unit transfer to Saskatoon Research and Development Centre
item.description: Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada (AAFC) confirms that for the 2027 growing season, the Seed Increase Unit (SIU) will operate out of both the Indian Head Research Farm and Saskatoon Research and Development Centre. This will support an orderly transition of the program to Saskatoon in 2028.

item.description: Small craft harbours are vitally important to coastal communities and to Canada’s fishing economies. In the Arctic, these harbours serve as critical community marine infrastructure that enhance safety, improve access and contribute to Canada’s broader Arctic sovereignty.

item.title: The Royal Canadian Air Force partners with Fanshawe College to deliver training
item.description: The Royal Canadian Air Force (RCAF) has partnered with Fanshawe College to deliver aviation maintenance training starting in January 2027. Through this partnership, the civilian college will deliver and maintain a Transport Canada-approved academic curriculum at the Canadian Forces School of Aerospace Technology and Engineering (CFSATE) at Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Borden.

item.title: Canada, Ukraine and Norway conclude conference on returning Ukrainian children, detained civilians and prisoners of war
item.description: The unlawful deportation and forcible transfer of Ukrainian children, the unlawful detention of civilians, and the treatment of prisoners of war are among the gravest consequences of Russia’s unprovoked and unjustifiable full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

item.title: Tribunal Initiates Expiry Review—Certain Small Power Transformers from Chinese Taipei and Korea
item.description: The Canadian International Trade Tribunal today initiated an expiry review (RR-2026-007) of its finding made on December 24, 2021, in inquiry NQ-2021-003, to determine if the expiry of the finding is likely to lead to continued or resumed dumping of certain small power transformers from Chinese Taipei and Korea and is likely to result in injury to the domestic industry.

item.title: National Film Board of Canada featured in the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art’s inaugural film program. Landmark films by Norman McLaren, Arthur Lipsett, Jean-Claude Labrecque and Theodore Ushev are among 19 NFB titles selected for stunning new museum experience in Los Angeles.
item.description: The National Film Board of Canada (NFB) has been chosen to be part of the inaugural film program at the new Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in Los Angeles, where 19 NFB works will be featured in continuous screenings in the museum’s two theatres. Founded by George Lucas and Mellody Hobson, the museum opened its doors on September 22.

item.title: Public hearing on Pickering Nuclear Generating Station and Waste Management Facility
item.description: Ottawa, Ontario – Part 2 of a 2-part public hearing held by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission (CNSC) will take place from October 6 to 9, 2026, to consider an application from Ontario Power Generation (OPG) to renew the power reactor operating licence for the Pickering Nuclear Generating Station (PNGS) and the waste facility operating licence for the Pickering Waste Management Facility.
